title: Probabilistic Calibration Is a Trainable Capability in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.11845v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Language models are increasingly used in settings where outputs should follow an intended distribution, yet their generation probabilities are often poorly calibrated to it. In many such requests the distribution is implicit and the valid outputs cannot be listed in advance, so the task cannot be passed to an external random number generator. We study whether this capability can be improved directly through fine-tuning. Concretely, we fine-tune language models on synthetic prompts that require sampling from mathematical distributions, and compare two Calibration Fine-Tuning variants: a soft-target method that converts the desired output distribution into trie-derived next-token targets, and a hard-target method that trains on sampled completions from the same target distribution. translated_title: 概率校准是语言模型中一种可训练的能力
translated_abstract: 语言模型越来越多地被应用于输出需要遵循预期分布的场景，但其生成概率与该分布的校准程度往往较差。在许多此类请求中，分布是隐式的，且有效的输出无法事先列举，因此该任务无法交给外部随机数生成器来完成。我们研究了这种能力能否通过微调直接得到提升。具体而言，我们在需要从数学分布中采样的合成提示上对语言模型进行微调，并比较了两种校准微调（Calibration Fine-Tuning）变体：一种是将目标输出分布转换为基于前缀树（trie）导出的下一词元目标的软目标方法，另一种是在从同一目标分布中采样得到的完整输出上进行训练的硬目标方法。在涵盖四个系列的12个模型上，两种方法都在保留分布族和未见参数上显著提升了结构化采样的保真度。
tldr: 该论文提出校准微调（包括软目标与硬目标两种变体），证明语言模型从隐式分布中进行采样的概率校准能力可以通过微调直接训练获得，并在12个模型上显著提升了结构化采样的保真度。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates that probabilistic calibration—the ability to sample from implicit target distributions—is a trainable capability of language models, achieved through two Calibration Fine-Tuning variants (soft-target and hard-target) that substantially improve structured-sampling fidelity across 12 models.
